name: Cookie banner
summary: Use the Cookie banner to ask for consent to non-essential cookies and confirm the choice without blocking access to the service.
whenToUse: Use when a service sets analytics, advertising or other non-essential cookies that require a user choice.
Show the banner until the user accepts or rejects non-essential cookies, then show a short confirmation message.
whenNotToUse: Do not ask for consent for cookies that are strictly necessary to provide the service.
Do not prevent users from accessing the service while waiting for a decision.

anatomy.name: Region
anatomy.description: A labelled region contains the current cookie message and uses data-nosnippet.

anatomy.name: Heading and explanation
anatomy.description: A concise heading and body explain which optional cookies are requested and why.

anatomy.name: Choice controls
anatomy.description: Equivalent accept and reject buttons are accompanied by a cookie-preferences link.

anatomy.name: Confirmation message
anatomy.description: After a choice, a replacement message confirms it and can be dismissed.

variants.name: Consent question
variants.use: Ask the user to accept or reject non-essential cookies.

variants.name: Choice confirmation
variants.use: Confirm a stored cookie choice and provide a way to hide the message.

behaviour: Application code must store the preference, apply it before setting non-essential cookies and replace the question with a confirmation message.
Both accept and reject actions must work without client-side JavaScript, for example as ordinary form submissions.
Do not re-display the question on every page after the service has stored a valid preference.
accessibility: Give the region a concise accessible name such as “Cookie banner”.
Make accept and reject actions equally prominent and keyboard operable.
Move focus only when testing shows it helps; do not unexpectedly trap or steal focus.
content: Name the service and explain the purpose of the optional cookies in plain language.
Use explicit action labels such as “Accept analytics cookies” and “Reject analytics cookies”.
Link to a page where users can review and change their preference.
